title: Playing with Machito: 'Cubop City'
summary: He and Brew Moore front Machito's band and record 'Cubop City' for Roost.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Yeah, that's what they billed it as. But of course, even during the Birdland years, you used to play the Roost.
Oh yeah.
Birdland reminded me of Machito, and of course, you recorded and played with Machito.
Machito, yeah.
And that was in the Forties. What can you say about that whole thing?
Oh, that was great. Playing with Machito was very nice, because he had a hell of a band at that period at that time. Brew Moore and I used to play in front of the band.
"Cubop City," right?
Yeah, right. And then we went into Bop City when they opened Bop City up, and we worked with the Machito
McGhee (12/1) - 4
and...
I guess that's how the tune got its name.

"Cubop City," yeah. So it was very nice. I enjoyed playing with Machito and them. They were very nice. I liked Mario; he's a very nice person. It was Teddy Reig that recorded that "Cubop City" and so on.
Right. He was with Roost Records then.

Yeah, he was with Roost Records. I don't know who's got it out now, but... What's his name, one of the Spanish cats the other day came by and brought me a copy of it that he had, showed me a copy of it that he had, of "Cubop City" with me and Brew Moore.
That's a recent LP version of it?
Yeah. It ain't the one that I heard before. But I guess just whoever decided to put it out, just put it out, you know. They don't give a damn.
Well, maybe what you heard was something from one of the broadcasts.
Yeah, well, that's...
You know, these bootlegs are coming out, and maybe that wasn't even the original...
Yeah. Tony Williams in England is a stone pirate.
Heh-heh...
McGhee (12/1) - 5
A real stone pirate, boy. He don't give up nothin' if he can keep from it.
